data.title: US goods trade deficit widens sharply in October
data.description:
The US trade deficit in goods widened sharply in October as an AI infrastructure buildout continued to draw in imports at a rapid clip, potentially putting trade on course to again subtract from economic growth in the fourth quarter.

The goods trade shortfall increased 10.7%, or $14.4 billion to $149.5 billion last month, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the goods deficit at $133 billion.

Goods imports shot up $21.1 billion to $365.3 billion. Exports of goods increased $6.7 billion to $215.8 billion.

The government reported on Wednesday that trade sliced off 3.21 percentage points from gross domestic product growth in the third quarter. The drag was, however, more than offset by robust growth in consumer spending and business investment in equipment, mostly AI-related.

The economy grew at a 4.3% annualized rate last quarter after expanding at a 2.2% pace in the April-June period. Trade has not contributed to gross domestic product growth for four straight quarters, reflecting strong domestic demand.

data.title: French Economy Slips Into Recession as Exports Sag — WSJ
data.description:
By Matthew Dalton

PARIS — The French economy tipped into a recession in the third quarter as summer heat waves slowed Airbus's factories, complicating the government's plans to narrow its yawning budget deficit.

Gross domestic product fell 0.2% in the third quarter after declining slightly in the second quarter, French statistics agency Insee said Friday. Economists define a recession as two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth.

France faces a morass of economic problems: anemic consumer spending, weak investment, an economy highly reliant on public spending and an export sector that is acutely exposed to the fortunes of Airbus, the aeronautics giant based next to Toulouse.

Punishing heat waves in July pushed temperatures inside Airbus factories to over 104 degrees Fahrenheit, according to union officials. Airbus slowed production of its A330 and A321 models, French authorities said, dragging down France's overall exports by 1.6%.

The government is proposing nearly EUR50 billion, equivalent to $55 billion, in budget savings to lower its deficit to 5% of GDP next year. The deficit this year is forecast to hit 5.5% of GDP, the largest in the eurozone. That threatens to stunt growth even more for an economy in which public spending accounts for around 57% of GDP, among the highest in the developed world.

Data coming in since the end of the quarter showed that France's domestic spending was weaker than expected, said Pauline Meinzel, an economist at Insee.

"Foreign trade is declining and we have domestic demand growth that is zero in the third quarter," she said.

France typically enjoys a construction boom ahead of local elections as mayors seek to curry favor with voters through public works, Meinzel said. That dynamic helped boost local spending before the most recent votes in March of this year on a host of big-ticket projects, from a tram extension in Marseille that cost EUR320 million to a new sports complex south of Paris at EUR100 million. Local government spending in total jumped 3.4% in 2025.

"Now, we're in a period of transition; the teams have just been re-elected," she said. "We're really seeing a sharp decline in investment in public works."

The decline in public spending threatens to sow further discontent among French voters ahead of next year's presidential elections and is likely to help Marine Le Pen's antiestablishment candidacy.

data.title: The Week in Oil: Crude on Track for Weekly Gains As Middle East Attacks Worry Market
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni

Here is a look at what happened in oil markets during the week of Nov. 23-27 and what traders will be watching in the days ahead.

OVERVIEW: Oil prices are on track for weekly gains on Friday after three consecutive weekly losses as continuing attacks on Middle Eastern shipping and Saudi infrastructure raised regional supply concerns. Front-month Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, is down 0.3% to $96.35 a barrel, while WTI futures rise 1.5% to $84.95 a barrel.

MACRO: Major U.S. indexes are poised to finish higher after a volatile week marked by AI jitters. "Stock markets around the world are hoping to put the recent turmoil behind them, staging a decent rebound as the week and month draw to a close," said XM analyst Raffi Boyadjian. "The shortened trading week in the United States due to the Thanksgiving holiday has likely helped in restoring some calm to equity markets."

This week's economic data indicated persistent inflation, resilient growth, and a solid labor market. Focus now shifts to the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision next month, with traders already pricing in a 25-basis-point hike.

GEOPOLITICAL RISKS: With no meaningful progress in U.S.-Iran negotiations, regional tensions remain high. Continued attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman have kept maritime security and potential supply disruptions in focus.

Oil supplies have remained largely unaffected, according to Commerzbank analysts. However, that could change if Saudi Arabia is forced to reduce oil exports through Ras Tanura, especially as Houthi militants also threaten export terminals on the Red Sea.

Earlier this week, the Houthis claimed an attack on Ras Tanura, which is Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery. Meanwhile, a separate strike on the country's Jazan refinery sparked a fire and temporarily halted some operations, while a drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians.

SUPPLY AND DEMAND: Middle Eastern oil flows remain significantly below prewar levels, with Strait of Hormuz transits at just 31% of the preconflict baseline, according to preliminary data from Kpler.

Iraqi crude exports remain relatively strong despite delays to some November and December shipments, which Kpler attributed to oversold cargoes rather than falling production. Still, the delays have raised concerns over the reliability of prompt Middle Eastern supply, highlighting the market's sensitivity to short-term disruptions even in an otherwise well-supplied regional market, said Alex Booth, head of research at the data provider.

In the U.S., crude oil inventories rose for a third consecutive week as refineries increased capacity utilization, according to the latest Energy Information Administration data. Gasoline and distillate fuel stocks also climbed.

WHAT'S AHEAD: Attention now turns to Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, with some analysts expecting the group to hold current production quotas steady through January. With existing production agreements approaching their year-end deadline, key members of the group must decide how much oil each country can sustainably produce, and how much the cartel should collectively pump next year.

"It is quite possible that Sunday's OPEC+ meeting will end without a final decision and that current production quotas will initially remain in place, as OPEC delegates have indicated," said Commerzbank analyst Barbara Lambrecht. "With the exception of Iraq, production in most OPEC+ countries remains well below existing quotas, while some countries, including Russia, are unable to raise output any further."

Investors will also be watching for Saudi Arabia's official selling prices, which are set to be disclosed next week.

On the U.S. economic calendar, the ISM manufacturing and services PMI readings will provide further insight into the strength of the economy, while Jolts, ADP employment and weekly jobless claims will offer clues on labor market conditions ahead of Friday's November nonfarm payrolls report.

data.title: Wall Street's Black Friday Bounce Could Set Record: Market Strategist Sees ‘Beach Ball’ Rally Ahead
data.description:
Key points:
  • Detrick said stocks are extremely oversold and could see a "beach ball” rally into year-end.
  • A "beach ball” rally is a sharp, fast rebound in stock prices after a heavy sell-off, like the one seen over the past month.
  • Interactive Brokers' Jose Torres said the Fed is most likely "one and done" on hikes, though markets price a possible January hike.

Ryan Detrick, chief market strategist at Carson Group, said on Friday that he sees room for a “beach ball” rally in U.S. stocks through year-end, with the market's rebound putting Black Friday on track for its strongest performance ever.

Meanwhile, Interactive Brokers’ senior economist Jose Torres expects the Federal Reserve to deliver one more rate hike before stopping. “We're one and done for hikes here,” he said.

"We are extremely oversold. Everybody knows that. But that beach ball is under the water. Now we're getting some good momentum," Detrick said in an interview with CNBC.

All Eyes On Black Friday

According to Detrick, Friday could deliver the best market Black Friday performance, even beating that of 1971. The S&P 500 rose 1.8% on Black Friday 1971, the best Black Friday since 1950, according to Yahoo Finance data. "After 1971's record Black Friday bounce in the stock market, the S&P gained another 11%, one of the stronger Decembers ever," Detrick said.

“Right now on Black Friday, this would be the best Black Friday ever, topping 1971's Black Friday.”

– Ryan Detrick, Chief Market Strategist, Carson Group

In pre-market trade, S&P futures were up about 1.7%, Nasdaq futures were up 2.1%, and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were up 1.3%. "I think we could have a beach ball rally the rest of this year," Detrick said.

A "beach ball” rally is a sharp, fast rebound in stock prices after a heavy sell-off, like the one seen over the past month.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY), which tracks the major index, rose to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory over the past day, while chatter dipped to ‘normal’ from ‘high’ levels.

Torres Says Fed Hikes Will Be 'One And Done'

Torres said he expects the Fed to raise rates once more and stop. "We're one and done for hikes here," he said.

However, according to CME FedWatch data, markets are pricing a 99% chance of a quarter-point hike at the December meeting, and about a 65% chance of another in January.

According to him, inflation in November and December "could actually be negative month over month on the consumer price index; that should get us down to the low threes to finish this year, and then in the vicinity of the Fed's target next year."

October's PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, rose 3.8% from a year earlier, in line with expectations. Core PCE rose 3.3%, above the 3.2% expected.

Torres also pointed to a strong economy and high consumer confidence. "We are set up here pretty positive for a year-end rally," he said.

"Things are still pretty solid in our opinion on the economy," Detrick added. According to him, investors are rotating. "People are paying a lot for staples, and they're throwing out their growth right now at historic rates," he said.

He added that the Carson Group is bullish on the healthcare segment and isn’t betting big on the technology sector.

The S&P 500 has shed massive gains amid the tech rout over the past month, now showing gains of around 4% for the year.

data.title: Generation Mining Completes $100 Million Convertible Note Offering
data.description:
Generation Mining Limited () (OTCǪB: GENMF) (“Gen Mining” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that, further to its news release dated September 14, 2026, it has completed a non-brokered private placement (the “Offering”) of unsecured, subordinated convertible notes of the Company (the “Convertible Notes”) with Canada Growth Fund Inc. (“CGF”) and Canada Infrastructure Bank (“CIB”, and together with CGF, the “Noteholders”) for aggregate gross proceeds of $100 million, pursuant to which each Noteholder subscribed for $50 million of Convertible Notes.

The financing will help advance construction of the Marathon Project and support the development of a new domestic supply of copper and palladium in Northwestern Ontario.

“We sincerely appreciate the support of Canada Growth Fund and the Canada Infrastructure Bank,” said Jamie Levy, President and Chief Executive Officer of Gen Mining. “CGF and the CIB have been invaluable partners in our mission to build Canada’s next critical minerals mine. Their commitment to the Marathon Project reflects a shared focus on securing a domestic supply of copper and palladium for Canada.”

The Convertible Notes, the issuance of which was approved at a special meeting of shareholders of the Company held on November 26, 2026, are convertible into an aggregate of up to 111,111,111 Common Shares at an initial conversion price of $0.90 per Common Share, subject to anti-dilution adjustments for any share splits, consolidations, reclassifications and dividends paid in Common Shares. The Convertible Notes will bear interest at a rate of 9.0% per annum. Interest will be calculated and payable in cash semi-annually in arrears, to the extent that the distribution conditions under the senior secured project finance facility of the Company (the “Senior Facilities”), once in place following settlement and execution of final documentation, do not restrict such cash payment. The Convertible Notes will mature on the earlier of: (i) November 27, 2037; or (ii) if the Senior Facilities and the subordinated debt facility of $200 million with CIB (the “CIB Facility”) have been repaid in full, including through refinancing, then on the later of: (A) November 27, 2033; and (B) 12 months after the repayment of the Senior Facilities and the CIB Facility.

Additional shares may be issuable upon conversion of payment-in-kind interest. For additional information about the Convertible Notes, please refer to the Company’s management information circular dated October 19, 2026, available under the Company’s issuer profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca.

The proceeds from the Offering will be used by the Company to fund the development, construction and operation of the Company’s 100%-owned Marathon Copper-Palladium Project (the “Marathon Project”), together with associated general and administrative and financing costs.

The Offering remains subject to final approval of the Toronto Stock Exchange (“TSX”).

CGF-Related Disclosure Required under the Early Warning System

Immediately prior to the Offering, CGF had ownership and control over 138,950,000 Common Shares, representing approximately 19.8% of the issued and outstanding Common Shares on a non-diluted basis. Immediately after the completion of the Offering, CGF has ownership and control over (i) $50 million principal amount of Convertible Notes, initially convertible into an aggregate of up to 55,555,555 Common Shares, representing approximately 7.9% of the issued and outstanding Common Shares on a non-diluted basis and (ii) 138,950,000 Shares, representing approximately 19.8% of the issued and outstanding Common Shares on a non-diluted basis. The Convertible Notes are subject to a blocker feature, which prohibits the issuance of Common Shares upon the conversion of the Convertible Notes where such issuance would result in CGF, together with its affiliates, holding more than 19.9% of the issued and outstanding Common Shares. Conversion of the Convertible Notes in excess of the 19.9% threshold will be cash settled by the Company.

CGF acquired the Convertible Notes for investment purposes and not with a view to materially affecting control of the Company. Depending upon market conditions and other factors, including pursuant to certain rights granted to CGF under the investor rights agreement dated as of September 21, 2026, entered into between CGF and the Company, CGF may, from time to time, acquire or dispose of additional securities of the Company, in the open market, by private agreement or otherwise, or acquire interests in or enter into related financial instruments involving a security of the Company.

This portion of this news release is being issued pursuant to National Instrument 62-103 – The Early Warning System and Related Take-Over Bid and Insider Reporting Issuers. A copy of CGF’s early warning report with respect to the Offering will be filed on SEDAR+ ( www.sedarplus.ca ) promptly, and, in any event, within two business days from the date hereof. For more information or to obtain a copy of the report, please contact Mathieu St-Amand, Senior Manager, Public Relations and Government Affairs, Canada Growth Fund Investment Management, at +1 (514) 925-1500. CGF has a registered office located at 79 Wellington Street West, Suite 3000, Toronto, Ontario, M5K 1N2.

The head office of the Company is located at 100 King Street West, Suite 7010, Toronto, Ontario M5X 1B1.

Generation Mining Limited ( | OTCǪB: GENMF) is a Canadian critical minerals development company focused on building the Marathon Copper-Palladium Project in Northwestern Ontario. The Company has commenced construction of the Marathon Project, one of Canada’s largest undeveloped copper-palladium deposits and a future domestic source of copper, palladium, platinum, gold and silver.

The Marathon Project is expected to be a long-life, low-cost mining operation producing critical minerals essential to electrification, clean energy technologies and emissions reduction. data.title: Gold gains about 3% as dollar rally stalls, equities stabilise
data.description:
Key points:
  • Don't see gold easily back to $5,000/oz, analyst says
  • Shares bounce after bruising month
  • Spot gold gained 4% weekly
  • Spot silver up nearly 7%

By Ashitha Shivaprasad

Gold prices rose about 3% on Friday, recovering from a more than one-year low hit earlier this week, with the market supported by a pause in the dollar's advance and calmer equity markets.

Spot gold jumped 2.8% to $3,664.97 per ounce by 1251 GMT, after it touched its lowest level since August 2025 on Wednesday. The rebound has set it on track for a 4% gain this week.

US gold futures for December delivery gained 3.6% to $3,663.80 per ounce.

"After days of declines, buyers returned to the market. Technology and AI stocks seem to have stabilised after the recent selloff, which is positive for gold because the market rout had forced some investors to liquidate bullion positions to raise cash and cover losses in other positions," said Carlo Alberto De Casa, external analyst for Swissquote.

"I don't see gold easily back to $5,000, but I see good chances that the price could return to $4,000-$4,200."

The US dollar took a breather after scaling a 22-month peak earlier this week. A softer dollar makes dollar-priced metals less expensive for holders of other currencies.

Equities steadied as they neared the end of a bruising month, with a US holiday lull giving some respite from AI jitters.

The US economy grew much faster than initially estimated in the third quarter, while inflation accelerated in October, data showed on Wednesday. These reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise rates next month and again in early 2027. (FEDWATCH)

Rising interest rates diminish gold's appeal by boosting returns on competing interest-bearing assets.

Meanwhile, physical gold demand in key Asian hubs improved this week, with jewellery and investment buying picking up in India, while strong retail purchases in China kept local premiums firm.

Spot silver climbed 5.7% to $43.88 per ounce, platinum gained 3.6% to $1,336.96 and palladium rose 3.5% to $903.79 per ounce. All three metals were on track for weekly gains.

data.title: BAE Systems Wins $6 Bln Deal To Supply Over 400 CV90 Combat Vehicles To Five Nations
data.description:
ARLINGTON (dpa-AFX) - BAE Systems plc (BA.L), a British aerospace and defence company, Friday said it has secured contracts worth $6 billion to supply more than 400 CV90 combat vehicles to Finland, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Norway and Sweden under a joint procurement agreement.

The orders cover the CV9035 MkIV Nordic Edition and mark the first time five countries have joined forces under a single procurement deal.

The contracts also include support systems such as training, spare parts, technical documentation, special tools and test equipment.

The company said production will involve suppliers across the five participating countries, helping strengthen regional industrial capabilities and security of supply.

'This procurement demonstrates the strength of the Nordic and allied cooperation, and it underscores the trust placed in the CV90 family - now expanded with Lithuania - as the backbone of modern, highly capable, mechanized forces,' said Tommy Gustafsson-Rask, general manager at BAE Systems Hägglunds. 'The CV9035 MkIV Nordic Edition combines combat-proven performance with the latest digital, protection and lethality upgrades, ensuring our customer nations can operate seamlessly together for decades to come.

On the LSE, BAE Systems shares rose more than 2% to 1,936.50p on Friday.
